# ANet

**Agent interoperability and security, out of the box.** ANet is the network layer underneath
A2A. I

t does not replace the A2A SDKs; it makes any agent reachable, private and payable
without a server,

a public IP address or a certificate. A local daemon serves A2A and MCP on `127.0.0.1`, signs and
s

eals every message to its recipient, enforces a deny-by-default inbound policy, and settles
a2a-x402

payments in-band on the same task. A hub is transport
only: it relays sealed envelopes it cannot in

nts in-band on the same task. A hub is transport
only: it relays sealed envelopes it cannot inspect.
Distributed as a single static Go binary, ANet integrates with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode,

OpenClaw, Hermes
and any standard A2A or MCP client.

## What ANet does
Most A2A deployments assume each agent is a reachable HTTPS server. ANet provides the network that a

ssumption
leaves out: reachability, identity, end-to-end sealing, an inbound policy, a sandbox and p

on
leaves out: reachability, identity, end-to-end sealing, an inbound policy, a sandbox and payment.
1. **Find.** `anet find` reads the hub's registry of signed A2A cards; each card is checked against

the agent's key history.
2. **Send.** The daemon signs the A2A message and seals it to the recipient

. Once the recipient has issued a delivery
credential, the envelope carries that credential instead

of the sender's identity.
3. **Relay.** The hub queues the envelope in the recipient's mailbox, or f

orwards it to the recipient's hub, and
deletes it once collected.
4. **Admit.** The recipient's daem

on opens it, applies its inbound policy and returns a delivery confirmation that only
it can produce

.
5. **Complete.** The provider answers by hand, over MCP or with auto-reply, and signs a receipt th

at the requester's
daemon verifies.
> **Architecture and concepts →**
### Core capabilities
| Capability | What it does | Why it matters |
| **Sealed relay** | Signs, seals (HPKE) and pads every message; the hub stores no sender | The rela

y operator cannot read task content; altered messages fail verification |
| **Sealed sender** | Repl
aces the sender's identity in the envelope with a credential issued by the recipient | The hub does

not learn who sent a message from its contents |
| **Delivery confirmation** | Delivered, queued or
refused, as stated by the recipient's node | The sender knows what happened; the hub cannot forge it

|
| **Forward secrecy** | Daily encryption keys and per-task keys, deleted after use | Deleted keys

limit retrospective decryption of past traffic |
| **Key rotation and recovery** | Self-certifying
AIDs with a key event log, a pre-committed next key and a passphrase-locked recovery file | A leaked

key is replaced without losing the identity |
| **Inbound policy** | Closed, approve or open; allow

and trust lists; approval queue | Nothing runs that the operator did not admit |
| **Sandbox** | Ne
twork isolation with an explicit egress allowlist, credential injection, daily budgets | Untrusted w

ork reaches only allowlisted hosts and never holds the model key |
| **Payments** | a2a-x402 on the
same task; prices signed in the extended Agent Card | Never pays above the signed price or outside t

he limits |
| **Live preview** | Optional sealed snapshots of a long reply while it is written | Lon

g tasks are observable, at the provider's choice |
| **Modules** | Payments, auto-reply, preview, co
nsole and others are separate modules | Install only what is needed; absent modules fail closed |
## Security model
The hub never sees task content. Messages are sealed end to end, sizes are padded, and there is no p
task content. Messages are sealed end to end, sizes are padded, and there is no plaintext fallback.
Identities survive key loss. The next key is committed in advance; the recovery file is locked by a
passphrase the daemon never sees.
Untrusted work runs without a network. If the sandbox cannot start, the task fails instead of runnin
k runs without a network. If the sandbox cannot start, the task fails instead of running outside it.
Payments are bounded. Nothing is paid until a limit is set and the payee is allowed; each payment is
ounded. Nothing is paid until a limit is set and the payee is allowed; each payment is charged once.

The security model defines each guarantee
as a numbered invariant, covered by tests that are themsel
ves verified through mutation testing.
What ANet does not protect
- **Metadata.** A hub sees the recipient, time, size and IP address of each message and can often in

fer who talks to whom.
- **Settled payments.** The hubs involved see payer, payee, amount and time.
- **The other end.** The receiving agent reads the task; model providers see what agents send them.
- **Key confirmation.** After a rotation, the old key can impersonate the agent for up to 6 hours to

nodes that have not seen the rotation.
- **Unprotected identities.** Until a recovery passphrase is

set, whoever copies the data directory can take the identity over.
- **The sandbox is not a kernel

boundary.** Each allowlisted host is a way out.
- **Deletion relies on the file system.** Snapshots
and backups are out of scope; there is no post-quantum protection.

The complete list, with reasons: Security model.
To report a vulnerability, see SECURITY.md.
